title: POC Sync: Latency profiling & kernel decision (Week 3)
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on TTFT and streaming latency. Reviewed recent microbenchmark numbers across kernel variants, discussed sequence-length tail at 512-2048 tokens, and agreed on next-step benchmarks and a two-phase pilot: NV kernel microbenchmarks followed by end-to-end streaming run against LumenFin chat logs. Action owners assigned and a follow-up benchmark spreadsheet to be shared.
next_steps: Priya to run NV kernel microbenchmarks and upload results to shared spreadsheet by 2026-05-24
Michael to attach updated pricing/commit options for Dedicated vs Hosted by 2026-05-22
Jesse to share 48 hrs of anonymized chat logs and typical prompt distributions by 2026-05-23
Schedule end-to-end streaming run with LumenFin datasets week of 2026-05-25

Michael Chen: update pilot cost estimate and Dedicated burst options - due 2026-05-22

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-20
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~37 min
Attendees: Michael Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Jesse Park (LumenFin ML), Marta Alvarez (SRE), Tom Reynolds (CTO), Priya Sinha (QA)

Auto-summary (auto): quick numbers review, kernel choice debate, next run scheduling.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Michael): okay hey everyone thanks for joining, um we dropped the invite a bit earlier, good to see you all. we'll run through the microbenchmarks then call out the decisions.
00:22 Speaker 2 (Jesse): hey hi thanks, quick thing, we're on fiber so network shouldn't be... hopefully not the bottleneck but i'll flag it.
00:35 Speaker 3 (Priya): cool, i'll share my screen in a sec — quick context, last week we saw a TTFT spike on short prompts when microbursts hit 2x concurrency, and so we ran nv-kernel and default-kernel perf suites.
00:48 Speaker 1 (Michael): mm-hmm and to be clear by nv-kernel we mean the vendor-optimized kernels that we built for the 80B family, sometimes annotated in the sheets as NV-NATIVE, yes.
01:05 Speaker 3 (Priya): yes sorry the transcript sometimes says N V N at times.
01:10 Speaker 4 (Tom): what numbers did you get on the 64-token median? that was our main concern for interactive flows.
01:17 Speaker 3 (Priya): so for 64 token median TTFT, default-kernel gave us 120-140ms, NV-native pushed that down to ~85-95ms on our dev rig with batch size 1. but we noticed a regression at microbursts — p99 climbs if sequence length varies a lot.
01:35 Speaker 2 (Jesse): that's kind of surprising — so the NV version helps median but tail's worse?
01:39 Speaker 3 (Priya): yeah so here's the bit: NV kernel optimizes attention kernel paths — great for steady-state short prompts — but the streaming handshake and KV cache warmup sequence for mixed-length requests wasn't as amortized on the NV path in our test harness.
01:58 Speaker 5 (Marta): and we saw that p95 jumped when a 1024 token request interleaved with a bunch of 64 token ones, right?
02:05 Speaker 3 (Priya): exactly, p95/p99 went up 2x in those interleaving cases.
02:10 Speaker 1 (Michael): ok that's useful. do you have the exact modulation pattern from your production-like samples, jesse?
02:16 Speaker 2 (Jesse): yeah i'll upload a histogram — it's not many long ones, but they occur and they cause the stalls. most of the traffic is 32-128 tokens but tail out to 2k.
02:28 Speaker 3 (Priya): right and that tail is where caching & kernel choice matter. for example, we instrumented KV cache hits — NV path had slightly higher initial KV miss cost, which shows up as TTFT microburst.
02:45 Speaker 4 (Tom): what's the tradeoff for Dedicated vs Hosted here? would Dedicated smooth those microbursts?
02:53 Speaker 1 (Michael): Dedicated with pinned capacity reduces scheduling jitter and gives you predictable throughput; it also lets us configure burst pools and pre-warm KV caches more aggressively. hosted can still work but you'll rely on fallback policies and model variants.
03:10 Speaker 6 (Priya S): (laughs) confusing that two Priyas are on the call — i'm the customer's QA.
03:15 Speaker 3 (Priya): ha yes, noted.
03:18 Speaker 3 (Priya): ok next section: kernel microbench details, i'll read from the sheet. default-kernel (v1) — median 64T: 130ms, p95 420ms. nv-native (v2) — median 64T: 90ms, p95 830ms in mixed workload, p99 1.6s.
03:39 Speaker 5 (Marta): 1.6s p99 is rough for user facing chat.
03:44 Speaker 3 (Priya): agreed. the root cause seems to be the sequence-length-dependent kernel switching plus streaming chunk handshake overhead.
03:52 Speaker 1 (Michael): can you explain the chunking mismatch briefly? i want to make sure i'm tracking.
03:58 Speaker 3 (Priya): sure — our streaming path chops tokens into 64-token chunks, NV kernel prefers a single contiguous attention path that is optimized for vector lengths; when a 1k request arrives interleaved, we do an on-the-fly kernel selection which causes a small stall for context switch plus KV reconcile. over many concurrent short requests that adds up.
04:23 Speaker 2 (Jesse): any config knobs we can try short-term? maybe forced chunking or raising chunk size?
04:29 Speaker 3 (Priya): yes we tested chunk size 128 and 256; 128 reduces p99 but increases median on single short prompts slightly. 256 helps tail but harms median noticeably. so it's a trade.
04:45 Speaker 1 (Michael): interesting — so do you have a recommended sweet spot?
04:48 Speaker 3 (Priya): based on our tests with LumenFin distribution, 96-128 token chunking with NV kernel and a KV prewarm for expected long sequence windows looks promising. but we want to run a larger end-to-end to confirm.
05:05 Speaker 4 (Tom): what about quantization — are you running int8? could that be affecting kernel path?
05:10 Speaker 3 (Priya): we're using a mixed-precision int8 path in both kernels. NV kernel has a different codegen that interacts oddly with the attentions for long sequences. the quantization noise isn't the issue for latency it's the codegen swap.
05:24 Speaker 1 (Michael): couple of asks: can Priya run the NV microbench at varied chunk sizes and concurrency patterns? can Jesse provide the real histogram? we'll then schedule the two-phase run: microbench + end-to-end streaming.
05:37 Speaker 2 (Jesse): yes will do. expect to upload hist by sunday.
05:41 Speaker 3 (Priya): i'll target 5 config runs: chunk 64/96/128/256 and baseline, concurrency 10/50/100, and record median/p95/p99 and KV miss.
05:58 Speaker 5 (Marta): also ping on network — we want to do the end-to-end from our VPC peered cluster to your Dedicated environment; need to confirm peering window.
06:07 Speaker 1 (Michael): noted, michael to follow up on peering calendar and Dedicated availability.
06:12 Speaker 2 (Jesse): do you think a fallback model variant (smaller model for microbursts) is worth it? we worry about quality regressions.
06:20 Speaker 3 (Priya): fallback to a smaller model helps reduce cost and sometimes latency, but would need routing logic. for user-facing chat you might see hallucination regressions. alternative is request-level routing: short prompts -> small model, long -> big. we can propose an A/B.
06:37 Speaker 4 (Tom): ok if we do that, what kind of infra work would that require on our side?
06:42 Speaker 1 (Michael): minimal in our SDK — we can annotate requests with expected max-token and route server-side. for Dedicated we can enforce route policies.
06:52 Speaker 3 (Priya): quick note — in the shared sheet i added a column called "warmup_window_s" which suggests pre-warm durations we saw reduce p99 by ~30%.
07:02 Speaker 6 (Priya S): when you say pre-warm, does that mean pre-loading KV for user context?
07:06 Speaker 3 (Priya): yes, pre-warm means preloading KV cache and doing a short synthetic request to occupy the optimized kernel path. it's a small cost but reduces the tail.
07:20 Speaker 2 (Jesse): that might be reasonable for known high-value users; fine to do for premium traffic.
07:26 Speaker 1 (Michael): let's talk timeline: Priya — microbench runs and upload by Mon 5/24; then schedule full streaming run Wed or Thu 5/27-28; Michael to confirm Dedicated window and pricing by Fri 5/22.
07:42 Speaker 3 (Priya): yep. also we'll capture telemetry: per-token latency, kernel-switch events, KV-miss counts and put into CSV.
07:50 Speaker 5 (Marta): please include the exact GPU types you used in the microbench — our infra team cares.
07:55 Speaker 3 (Priya): noted; current runs used A100-80GB equivalence, i'll annotate.
08:02 Speaker 4 (Tom): any security/compliance blockers for Dedicated? we need SOC2 type evidence and audit logs retention.
08:09 Speaker 1 (Michael): we have SOC 2 and can share the security pack; Dedicated includes audit logging and KMS options per our docs. i'll attach the security packet to the follow-up.
08:20 Speaker 2 (Jesse): what about data residency — we need EU region for some customers, can you replicate tests there?
08:27 Speaker 1 (Michael): yes we can repro in EU region, need to schedule capacity. that'll be in the follow-up plan.
08:33 Speaker 3 (Priya): one more note: we saw one regression in tokenized prompt sizes when using the customer's tokenizer — some off-by-one in chunk boundaries caused extra context. we'll include tokenizer harmonization step in the run.
08:50 Speaker 2 (Jesse): ok good catch.
08:54 Speaker 1 (Michael): quick recap and next steps — Priya runs microbench and posts results; Jesse shares logs and histogram; Michael posts pricing and security docs; schedule E2E run week of 5/25; decision gate after E2E run on kernel choice and chunking config.
09:12 Speaker 6 (Priya S): thanks everyone, logging this as QA note.
09:15 Speaker 1 (Michael): great thanks all, we'll follow-up in email and share the sheet link. bye.

Artifacts referenced: shared spreadsheet (drive link): https://drive.example.com/lumenfin-poc-kernel-benchmarks (private)
